newsitem.title: AUSTRIA: Austria's Klima calls for hand gun ban.
newsitem.headline: Austria's Klima calls for hand gun ban.

text.p: Austrian Social Democrat Chancellor Viktor Klima has voiced support for a ban on hand guns just one week after a 15-year-old schoolboy shot his teacher dead with his father's revolver.
"It is shocking. I am for a ban on hand guns with few exceptions," Klima said in remarks published in Thursday's edition of Die Krone newspaper.

Klima's stand reflects growing concern worldwide over the availability of guns among the civilian population following the massacre of 35 people at a Tasmania tourist resort and the murder of 16 children and their teacher in a Scottish school.
Britain's newly-elected Labour Prime Minister Tony Blair said he hopes to introduce a blanket ban on all handguns by the summer, fulfilling a pledge he made last year after the killings in Scotland.
In Austria, Klima said access to pistols and revolvers for children and young people was far too easy.
"They obviously have the impression through the representation of violence, also on television, that one can solve problems through shooting," he said.
Interior Minister Karl Schloegl on Saturday announced plans to tighten gun laws with effect from July 1 to ensure that Austria's 330,000 registered gun owners keep their weapons in a secure place.

The opposition Greens have demanded a total ban on guns for private individuals. Far-right Freedom Party leader Joerg Haider said people needed to protect themselves but called for heavy penalties for owners who do not lock away their weapons.
Legislation already approved by parliament will make it more difficult for private individuals to acquire guns from July 1.

Under the new rules, applicants for a licence will be assessed for their suitability and, in the case of shotguns, it will no longer be enough to register the weapon at the shop where it is bought but must also be recorded by the police.
Schloegl said he also planned to take further steps to reduce the high number of weapons held illegally in Austria.
The sale of pump action shotguns was banned in Austria in 1995 after a sharp rise in murders committed with the guns, many of them by teenagers who killed members of their family.
